projections. The finite real frequency set is

  F={u_a-u_b : P_a B P_b is nonzero},
  B_alpha=sum_{u_a-u_b=alpha} P_a B P_b,
  B=sum_alpha B_alpha, B_alpha*=B_{-alpha},
  K=sum_alpha exp(alpha/2) B_alpha.                         (F)

When local s has degeneracies, P_a may have arbitrary rank; no basis inside
it is chosen and coincident frequencies are combined. The reference has no
effect on the local frequency set. A zero frequency is allowed.

Diagonalize the FULL joint state:
  rho=sum_i q_i^2 |i><i|, q_i>0,
and set
  beta_ij=log(q_i/q_j),
  c_alpha(i,j)=<i|B_alpha|j>.

For kappa real, put lambda=kappa/2 and define on ALL real x,y

  k_lambda(x)=x sinh x-lambda(cosh x-1),
  T_lambda(x,y)=x sinh y+y sinh x
                  -4lambda sinh(x/2)sinh(y/2),
  K_lambda(x,y)=T_lambda(x,y)/(2cosh((x-y)/2)).              (K)

The symbol K_lambda is a scalar kernel and is distinct from the physical
noise K in (F). It is finite at zero and at repeated/opposite points.

3. The exact complete identity

For ONE elementary Hermitian noise in any local and reference dimension,

  J_B-kappa E_B
   = 2 sum_{i,j} q_i q_j
       sum_{alpha,gamma in F} conjugate(c_alpha(i,j))
        K_{kappa/2}(beta_ij-alpha,beta_ij-gamma)
        c_gamma(i,j).                                    (G)

Both i=j and i!=j terms are included. This is an ordered-pair sum with the
factor TWO shown, not an unordered-pair sum with the same factor. Frequencies
of opposite sign and complex matrix elements must be retained. We now prove
(G), including the full physical potential, rather than postulate its sign.

3a. The stationary/root potential in frequency coordinates

Let P_sigma=-L_B(log sigma), where L_B is the Heisenberg adjoint of L_{*,B}.
Writing the physical D_B in its Hermitian plus skew-Hermitian parts shows
that the Hamiltonian trace against log rho is zero, but it generally has
a nonzero stationary-log trace. The following formula RETAINS that trace:

  P_sigma=d^(-1)[2 B s u B - {V_B,2 s u}/2]d^(-1).

For a product B_alpha* B_gamma put
m=(alpha+gamma)/2, h=(alpha-gamma)/2. If its local matrix element follows
the path b<-a->c, then alpha=u_a-u_b, gamma=u_a-u_c. Hence

  2s_a/(s_b+s_c)=exp(m)/cosh h,
  (s_b u_b+s_c u_c)/(s_b+s_c)=(u_b+u_c)/2+h tanh h.

The Lyapunov formula and the displayed P_sigma therefore give EXACTLY

  V_B=sum_{alpha,gamma} [exp(m)/cosh h] B_alpha* B_gamma,
  P_sigma=su
